watchlist.name: Citadel
watchlist.note: The hedge fund side of Ken Griffin's Citadel. The quants are mostly on the Global Quantitative Strategies team (GQS). Citadel tends to be fairly school-selective.

watchlist.name: Citadel Securities
watchlist.note: The market making arm of Citadel. The general perception is that the culture tends to be better at Citadel Securities vs Citadel LLC.

watchlist.name: Jane Street
watchlist.note: Founded by ex-SIG people. Tends to be more school-agnostic than other firms. General perception of JS is that it has a very comfortable and nerdy culture. Specializes in ETF market making, and uses OCaml as their primary programming language. Has big offices in London and Hong Kong. Opens roles in July.

watchlist.name: Hudson River Trading
watchlist.note: We thank Hudson River Trading for sponsoring the Northwestern University Fintech Club. Please apply via [this link](https://grnh.se/f4cuomjz1us) and your application will be linked to this Github repo. The Algo Dev role at HRT is essentially Quantitative Research. HRT's culture seems to be pretty similar to JS and pay is similar too. HRT has a bigger focus on ML with their dedicated HRT AI Labs. Known for recruiting UG QRs, and for very collegial culture.

Claude Campus Program — Builder Club leads & Campus Ambassadors

listings.title: Datathons (Women's Datathon, Summer Invitational, regional)
listings.eligibility: undergrads at US/Canada universities graduating Dec 2027 – Jun 2029
listings.note: Run with Correlation One. Women's Datathon is in February in Miami (all expenses paid, $15k prizes); Summer Invitational follows. Invite via application.

listings.title: NVIDIA Ignite (12-week pre-internship, first/second-years)
listings.eligibility: first- and second-year undergrads at US universities, historically underrepresented communities encouraged
listings.note: On-site in Santa Clara with travel and a housing stipend; software and hardware tracks. The 2026 edition took applications from mid-September to mid-October and was posted on NVIDIA's job board as 'NVIDIA 2026 Ignite Internships', so the next one is picked up automatically.

listings.title: Associate Software Developer Intern (ASDI) — formerly STEP
listings.eligibility: first- and second-year undergrads in CS or related fields
listings.note: Google renamed STEP to ASDI in 2025: a 12-week early-undergrad engineering internship with a mentor and a paired project. It's posted on Google Careers, historically Sep–Oct, and fills on a rolling basis; when it's live it appears in the internships list above as well. Search 'Associate Software Developer Intern' on the Students page.

listings.title: Explore Microsoft (first- and second-year internship)
listings.note: 12-week rotational internship across PM, engineering and design for early undergrads; posted on Microsoft's careers site in the fall and picked up here when live.

listings.title: BOLD Internship (non-technical, first/second-years)
listings.note: Business-side counterpart to ASDI for first- and second-years; search 'BOLD' on Google's Students page when the season opens.

listings.title: Women in Trading and Technology Internship (WiTTI)
listings.eligibility: sophomores (all identities welcome; built for women+ and nonbinary students)
listings.note: Paid 2–4 week winter program in NYC starting early January: Python/C++ projects, algo dev and SWE exposure. Last cycle's deadline was Oct 12; it's posted on HRT's job board when open.

listings.title: Fellowships: Discovery, Latitude, Momentum, Nexus
listings.eligibility: early undergrads; some tracks for women and underrepresented groups
listings.note: Short paid programs in New York introducing the firm; listed under D. E. Shaw's careers site.

listings.title: YC Internship Cohort — internships at YC startups
listings.note: One application to intern at YC companies, plus a student cohort with closed-door founder talks. The Summer 2026 round has closed; the page is re-read each run for the next one.

listings.title: First-Year Trading and Technology Program (FTTP)
listings.eligibility: first-year undergrads planning a STEM major
listings.note: A few days of classes and a team mock-trading game in the office; travel, accommodation and a daily stipend covered. No sponsorship requirements.

listings.title: Two Sigma student programs (Ignite, fellowships)
listings.note: Two Sigma's students page lists insight programs and fellowships for early undergrads.

listings.title: Fixed Income and Macro Central Bank Challenge
listings.note: Listed on Citadel's programs page; open the page for this year's dates.

listings.title: Terminal (Correlation One coding competition)
listings.note: Tower-defense-style algorithm competition; winners get access to job opportunities.

listings.title: IMC Prosperity (global trading challenge)
listings.note: Multi-round algorithmic + manual trading game each spring with cash prizes; look for 'Prosperity' on IMC's site.

listings.title: SIG Discovery Day and sophomore programs
listings.note: SIG's campus page lists discovery days and early-year programs (Bala Cynwyd, PA).

listings.title: Apply to Y Combinator (current batch)
listings.note: YC funds four batches a year (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall); standard deal is $500k. Fall 2026's on-time deadline was July 27; the next batch's deadline is read from this page each run.

listings.title: Jane Street Immersion Program (JSIP)
listings.eligibility: first- and second-year undergrads who experienced barriers to opportunity in computer science
listings.note: Multi-week summer software-engineering program in NYC; housing, travel and meals covered, plus a $12,500 scholarship per Fellow. Last cycle's deadline was Feb 8; second-years are read on a rolling basis, first-years in February.

listings.title: Ready Trader Go / trading challenges
listings.note: Optiver's student page lists its coding and trading competitions and insight days.

listings.title: Startup School (free online course)
listings.note: YC's self-paced course and founder-matching; no application, start any time.

listings.title: Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors
listings.note: Rolling applications; community-leadership program with events, Azure credits and training.

listings.title: Electronic Trading Challenge (ETC)
listings.note: Day-long programming contest in a simulated market, hosted at campuses through the fall; cash prizes. Sign-ups close about a week before each date.

listings.title: Ignite Women's Trading Program
listings.note: Invite-only week in New York in January: market-making overviews and trading exercises; travel and hotel covered. Past sign-ups ran through events.citadelsecurities.com/ignite.

listings.title: Meta University (engineering)
listings.eligibility: first- and second-year undergrads at four-year universities in the US, Canada or Mexico; underrepresented communities encouraged
listings.note: Paid ten-week summer internship (May–August): a few weeks of technical training, then project work with a Meta engineer as mentor. Applications usually open November–January and include a coding challenge; first-years need one college CS course, second-years two.

listings.title: Discover Citadel Securities
listings.note: Invitation-only two-day event in New York, London, Hong Kong or Singapore.

listings.title: Early Decision for Students
listings.eligibility: current students who want to finish their degree first
listings.note: Apply to YC while in school; if accepted you're funded now and your spot is held for a batch after you graduate. Pick 'a batch after the current one' on the application.

listings.title: Student Researcher Program
listings.note: Part- or full-time research projects with Google researchers; reviewed on a rolling basis, closes when projects fill.

listings.title: Conference Travel Grant
listings.note: Grant to support rising STEM talent attending conferences.

listings.title: Swift Student Challenge
listings.note: Build an app playground in Swift; winners get a year of Apple Developer Program membership and some are invited to WWDC. Submissions usually open in February.

listings.title: Google Summer of Code
listings.eligibility: 18+ students and beginners in open source
listings.note: Paid open-source projects with mentoring orgs; applications typically open in March.

listings.title: Trading Invitational
listings.note: Apply to compete; put trading skills to the test on-site.

listings.title: Trading Invitational

listings.title: Sophomore Internship

listings.title: MLH hackathon season

listings.title: Quant Invitational
listings.note: Invite-only 5-day research challenge in Miami, all expenses paid.

listings.title: Discover Citadel
listings.note: Two-day invitation-only event in New York (also London, Hong Kong, Singapore, Sydney) covering both Citadel and Citadel Securities.

listings.title: Meta Hacker Cup
listings.note: Annual algorithmic programming contest; qualification round usually in September, finals later in the year.

listings.title: MLH Fellowship
listings.note: 12-week remote program with several tracks (software engineering, production engineering, site reliability); cohorts run a few times a year with rolling applications.

listings.title: Imagine Cup
listings.note: Microsoft's global student startup/tech competition; registration usually opens in the fall.

listings.title: Explore CSR

listings.title: Inside HRT

listings.note: Few-day program with classes and mock trading across trading, SWE, and strategy & product tracks.

listings.title: INSIGHT

listings.note: Multi-day program in trading, software engineering, or strategy & product tracks. Apply to the office nearest you; travel covered.

listings.title: BRIDGE
listings.note: Day-long program on how the business works: Strategy & Product track (New York) or Institutional Sales & Trading (London offers both). Apply to the office nearest you.

listings.title: FOCUS

listings.note: Multi-day introduction to Jane Street for first-years; no finance background needed.
